label: Natural state determined to one end (ad unum): fixed by end-realization
term: natural state determined to one end (NaturalStateAdUnum n fitOf)
definition: NaturalStateAdUnum n fitOf: any two variation scenarios that agree on end-realization give the same natural state (the state factors through fitOf). The nature responds to the candidates only through whether they realize its end. Example: Lane 2b's D-directed nature, whose state records only which candidates realize D. Non-example: a natural state that records the candidates' full content, under which candidates that realize D equally still differ (the imitability-exemplar rival's modes). Sense restriction: this is determination to one end-content class (the end-realization feature fitOf). A nature determined to the good as such, such as the will as nature (ST I q.82 a.1, navigation only) or the imitability-exemplar rival's nature, is not ad unum in this sense; the record does not encode the claim that such a determination is also 'to one'.
note: Stipulative analyst notion (#2145 lane H3), attribution deferred. It is a typed reading of determinatio ad unum of a natural form (ST I q.19 a.4 second reason; q.59 a.1; navigation only). It enters only Lean-only lemmas (adUnumNaturalNotGoodGeneral, goodGeneralIsRationalUnderAdUnum). See docs/notes/causal-perfection-transfer.md, section 'Natural or rational appetite? The purity premises and the object of an original source's favouring'.
